title: Council Order 0015494: change of use of a farm-building addition to living quarters; whether a dwelling unit exists
jurisdiction: Alberta; accredited municipality not named in the order (respondent)
code_edition: Alberta Building Code 2014 (defined terms cited in the decision: Division A 1.1.1.1 and 1.4.1.2)
document_date: 2019-06-26 (Council Order 0015494); the underlying order is dated 2019-04-04

facts.text: The order dated 2019-04-04, issued under section 49 of the Safety Codes Act by the accredited municipality against the property owner, was varied; the owner was directed to submit a building permit application and drawings for the change of use of the shop to include living quarters.
The issue is an addition to a farm building possibly containing living quarters and whether a building permit is required for the change in use.

The safety codes officer attended on 2019-01-23 and observed a two-storey interior development that he considered residential; a large amount of stored furniture gave an impression of residential occupancy.
The addition contained two kitchens, three bathrooms with showers and toilets, two laundry rooms and a lift; the second level contained an emergency egress stairwell.
The question before the Tribunal is whether the building contains a dwelling unit as defined in the ABC; the decision notes people were sleeping in the building before the January inspection.
